problem: World models for navigation (e.g. NWM) are decoupled from their external planners (CEM/MPPI). The planner samples blindly in an unbounded continuous action space and must decode every candidate to pixels to score it with LPIPS, which is too slow (>500 s per plan) and unreliable for real-time robot control.
motivation: Foresight would let robots escape dead ends and avoid obstacles, but the sampling and pixel-decoding bottleneck makes world-model planning impractical on physical hardware. Discretizing intents into learned codebooks gives a bounded search space of plausible maneuvers. It also gives cheap uncertainty (entropy) and out-of-distribution (quantization error) signals that can be evaluated without decoding.
key_idea: Move the planner inside a discrete world action model: search over VQ-codebook kinodynamic and visual intents, rank them with a latent Kinematic-Perceptual Cost, and decode only the winner to continuous trajectories with flow matching.
insight: Discretization makes the search space bounded and physically plausible, and turns quantization error and token entropy into pixel-free collision signals. Table 2 shows the continuous VertiFormer (MPPI) gets 0% success with obstacles, while Hydra's DLP gets 8/10. Table 6 shows removing any of Cprior, Cvq or Cent increases collisions on both Spot and Jackal. Table 5 shows the image-goal cost hurts when the goal is not visible (80% -> 20% SR).
method: Early-fusion unified encoder: SD-VAE visual latents plus Fourier-featured poses and actions are broadcast and summed into one token stream, with modality masking and a cosine infilling curriculum. A 6/6-layer Transformer encoder-decoder outputs H intent tokens.
Asymmetric VQ bottleneck: modality-specific codebooks (visual 2048, pose 64, action 64), with a linear projection and deterministic MSE anchoring head for codebook stability.
Multimodal flow-matching decoders: rectified-flow DiT heads for image (50 NFEs), pose and action (10 NFEs); called only once for the elite trajectory.

Discrete Latent Planning: iterative CEM-like search (3 iterations, 18 samples, horizon 12). It seeds from an unbiased expert prior, adds EMA-smoothed Gaussian noise to the intent query, and applies top-K annealed Gumbel-max codebook sampling.

Kinematic-Perceptual Cost: J_KPC = C_geo + discounted sum of image-goal, expert-prior NLL, visual-token entropy, and VQ manifold-rejection (quantization error) terms, all computed in latent space except C_geo.

Path-following modes: classifier-free guidance in kinodynamic latent space (z̃ = z∅ + ω(zg − z∅)) and sub-goal/path sampling of prior-plus-codebook candidates scored by tracking cost or truncated Chamfer distance. Action chunking with temporal ensembling smooths execution.

setting.backbone: Hydra 143.29M-parameter Transformer encoder-decoder with VQ codebooks and DiT flow-matching heads (trained from scratch; frozen SD-VAE)
setting.training_data: Heterogeneous GNM-style robot navigation corpus (RECON, SCAND, SACSoN, TartanDrive), 100,355 samples / 157M tokens; unnormalized actions; 60 epochs
setting.observation: Monocular egocentric RGB history (8 steps, 224x224) plus poses and previous actions; goal image or pose/waypoints
setting.action_space: Predicted continuous pose/action trajectories (12 steps at 4 Hz) selected from discrete intent codes
setting.privileged: none (external waypoint guidance only in path-following mode)

numbers.extra: Inference offloaded to an A5000 workstation; plan time ~0.9s; SR = success in unobstructed / obstructed / corner-turn scenarios (out of 10)

numbers.eval_set_note: 100 clips of 16 s at 4 FPS from held-out RECON subset

numbers_note: No standard simulator benchmarks; all results are custom real-robot trials or offline datasets. Only selected rows of Table 3 are included (the paper's Table 3 covers other scenario/variant combinations too). Table 8 gives single-step image quality (DreamSim 0.1103, LPIPS 0.2809, PSNR 16.20) but is not entered.
results: Hydra plans in ~0.9 s versus >500 s for NWM/B (~500x faster) and achieves 10/10 (unobstructed) and 8/10 (obstructed and corner-turn) success. NWM gets 0/10 everywhere and VertiFormer 4/10, 0/10 and 0/10. As a local follower with sparse waypoints, it matches or exceeds GNM/ViNT/NoMaD success (e.g. 100% vs 0% on Long Distance), and its FVD (19.16) beats NWM/B (22.11).
limitations: Quantization error confuses visual complexity (foliage) with real obstacles, giving false positives, and may under-flag flat walls; pedestrians are erased by the 2048-entry visual codebook
Small real-world evaluation (10 trials per scenario, close-range ~8 m) with few baselines; planning mode fails on Long Distance (40%) due to latency, and goal-blind seeding misses near turns
Codebook size trades expressivity against search latency; deterministic VertiFormer is better on ADE/FDE and some traversal times
